groupings.description: Keep each extended grapheme cluster intact, including its combining marks and joined sequences. Supply UAX29/Intl.Segmenter boundaries; the standard-library resolver does not claim a complete Unicode segmenter.
Group whitespace-delimited orthographic tokens while retaining all spaces and punctuation. These tokens are not guaranteed semantic words in every language.
Use editor-supplied phrase boundaries. Each phrase moves as a whole and every supplied substring must concatenate exactly to the source text.
Use actual visual lines measured after loading the font and finalizing layout. Explicit source-preserving line boundaries are required; guessed wrapping is not accepted.
Use provisional sentence boundaries with punctuation preserved. Verify abbreviations, decimal separators and quotations before implementation.
Use paragraphs separated by blank lines, preserving all blank-line delimiters in their original order.
Use explicitly tagged semantic spans, such as a claim plus qualifier, number plus unit, or an indivisible named entity.
Make mechanical chunks of at most three consecutive orthographic tokens. These chunks aid pacing but are not inferred semantic phrases.
Treat the complete source text as one unit. All traversal orders collapse to the same activation order when there is only one unit.
Use exactly two editor-supplied contrast groups with source-preserving boundaries. Do not invent a comparison missing from the content.

traversals.description: Activate units in original source reading order; do not rearrange their source substrings or final layout.
Activate in reverse index order while keeping the original text and final reading arrangement unchanged.
Activate nearest to the center of the ordinal unit sequence first, then outward; break ties by original index. This is ordinal, not geometric center.
Activate from both ends of the ordinal sequence toward its center; break ties by original index.
Activate one-based odd positions first, then even positions; retain final text order.
Activate one-based even positions first, then odd positions; retain final text order.
Activate using a reproducible permutation from the declared seed. Reuse the same seed for repeatable previews and renders.
Activate by Euclidean distance of the final anchors from normalized canvas center, nearest first; resolve layout before ranking; tie by index.
Activate by ascending final anchor x+y for a diagonal scan; resolve layout before ranking; tie by index.
Activate by supplied semantic-priority values, highest first; missing priorities remain an unresolved requirement rather than being guessed.

temporals.description: Fast initial travel that decelerates to rest; curve v=1-(1-u)^3. Hold at the exact read pose, then fade out.
Symmetric acceleration and deceleration; curve v=u*u*(3-2*u). Finish entrance before beginning the reading interval.
Reserve the first 20 percent for a small reverse anticipation, then approach rest with cubic deceleration. Clamp bounded alpha/mask channels.
Use damped progress v=1-exp(-6*u)*cos(8*u), forced to one at u=1. Apply overshoot only to channels that allow it; do not duplicate an intrinsic family spring.
Advance the operator through five discrete progress steps, v=floor(5*u)/5, with the final step exactly one. This is a spatial progression, not a flashing luminance instruction.
Reach 70 percent progress by u=.4, pause until u=.58, then complete the remaining 30 percent by u=1.
Use a longer sine-out entrance, v=sin(pi*u/2), then stop all essential text motion for reading.
Combine cubic arrival with a small decaying ripple: v=1-(1-u)^3+.08*sin(4*pi*u)*(1-u), forced to one at the endpoint.
Advance at constant normalized progress v=u and stop at the exact final pose; suitable for mechanical scans and process-like motion.
Enter with cubic deceleration. During the middle of the reading interval, apply one optional small scale accent, peak 1.04, then return to one; use a stable alternative for dense or critical content.

compositions.description: Center the measured text block around canvas anchor (.5,.5). Keep the original reading order and derive actual widths and wraps from font metrics.
Place a left-aligned editorial block at anchor (.12,.45). Respect a safe inset and reserve space for adjacent visuals.
Place a left-aligned lower-third block at anchor (.12,.78), with a contrast backing when needed and enough room for descenders and captions.
Place a left-aligned upper-third block at anchor (.12,.22), reserving the remaining frame for the subject or supporting content.
Stack units vertically, centered at x=.5 and distributed over y=.18 to .83. Measure the complete height and reflow if the stack does not fit.
Distribute consecutive units alternately between two columns centered at x=.25/.75; each subsequent row advances .12 normalized y. Fit or paginate before anchors leave the frame.
Use two labeled comparison regions centered at x=.25/.75. At least two semantic groups are required; typography must not imply unequal data scales.
Place short units around a radius .27 circle centered at (.5,.5), with first angle -pi/2 and successive angles 2*pi*i/N. Keep the final orientation readable.
Place a callout around (.75,.25). If attached to an object, supply a measured screen/world anchor and a leader endpoint; do not fabricate tracking.
Place unit i at (.2+.6*i/max(N-1,1), .25+.5*i/max(N-1,1)). Use only short text and verify the diagonal reading hierarchy.
